path

The path: plan a walk to a goal, run its steps, change them, make a course, and find a source for each step.

This module plans a path to a goal and runs it. It imports from abhyasa.learner, abhyasa.models, abhyasa.sources and abhyasa.tutor. It has five parts:

  • Plan a walk: the planner, the walk from a paper, a text, a topic or a goal, the rabbit holes, and the readers of a step.
  • Run a walk step: the tutor note of a step, its check, and the notebook spec that runs in Leela.
  • Change a walk: the history of the changes, Undo, and the edits of the walk path.
  • Courses: a course to your goal, its stages, where you are and what comes next.
  • Find a source for each step: research on the web and in your folders, with the agent that gathers a passage for each idea.

The stored walk (journey, put_journey, walk_state) is in abhyasa.learner, and the checks of a web source are in abhyasa.sources. Research loads the explainer video of abhyasa.show when it needs it, because that module imports this one.

Import the modules that this module uses. The heavy ones load inside the functions that need them, so the import stays light.

Plan a walk

A walk and its path: an ordered list of steps, one concept each, that the learner can see and change. The module is abhyasa.path.

A learner often wants to learn more than one concept. “I want to learn how LLMs work” needs tokenizers, embeddings, attention, transformers and more, in a given order. A walk keeps that goal and that order on the learning shelf.

The planner (one model call) proposes the steps. It uses the concepts on the shelf when they fit. It makes new concepts for the topics that the shelf does not have. Then the learner can change the path: move, skip, mark as known, add and split steps.

A walk keeps the outcome of each check on its step, and walk_state counts them. A concept that the learner learns anywhere is known in each walk that has it. An old walk with no mode (a path, from before 0.0.16) becomes a topic walk once, in the background at the start of the app, with its progress (walk_path).

Change the steps

journey_step makes one change to one step: up, down, skip, known, todo or remove. journey_add adds a step at the end, or before another step. A step of a walk gets a short check.

The planner

The planner gets the goal and the learner profile as text. It also gets the concepts on the shelf that are near the goal or that the learner started. It returns the steps in order.

source

near_goal

def near_goal(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, goal:str, k:int=40, most:int=150
)->list:

(slug, name, floor) for the concepts that search finds for goal. A concept from another walk that search does not find stays out, so its old statement does not come back.

source

plan_prompt

def plan_prompt(
    goal:str, who:str='', known:tuple=(), srcmap:tuple=(), data:tuple=(), audience:str='', no_code:bool=False,
    asks:str=''
)->str:

The prompt that plans a path to goal. srcmap is the source_map of the sources that the goal names, and data the data entries (name, what) that a notebook can use. audience says who the walk is for, no_code asks for no code, and asks is what the learner asks for this plan. The sources, the data, the audience and the asks go in <source> markers, as data and not as instructions.

Who the walk is for, a request for no code, and what you ask for this plan go in the prompt only when you give them. The audience and your words are in <source> markers: they are data, not instructions.

p = plan_prompt('Teach agentic engineering', audience='people who do not write code', no_code=True, asks='Use only the notebook.')
assert all(x in p for x in ('Who the walk is for', 'people who do not write code', 'No code:', 'Use only the notebook.'))
assert not any(x in plan_prompt('Teach agentic engineering') for x in ('Who the walk is for', 'No code:', 'The learner asks'))
p

The source map

A goal can name its sources, such as course22p2 and fastbook. The Start box files them as chips. chip_docs gives the documents of each chip that is in the vault: a folder, a repo, a GitHub repo or one vault document. source_map gives the planner, for each chip, its root and up to 40 documents, each as its short title and its first heading. So the plan can name the document of each step.

source

source_map

def source_map(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, chips, most:int=40
)->list:

For each chip, its root and up to most (doc title, first heading), in path order.

source

chip_docs

def chip_docs(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, chips
)->list:

(root, docs) for each chip id that names vault documents (vault:, folder:, repo:, gh:, doc:, file:), in chip order. A file: chip gives only the document of that file. Other chips give nothing.

plan saves the walk. A step can name a known slug, or a known name or alias. Then it uses that concept and keeps its state. Each other step becomes a new concept, with the steps it needs as its prereqs. With sources, plan links each new concept to the passages that name it in the learner’s own sources. With a source map, each step also keeps the doc it comes from (only a title from the map), hands='notebook' for a step that builds part of the goal, what that notebook makes, and the data entries that it names. A step keeps only the fields that have a value.

source

plan

def plan(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, goal:str, who:str='', sources:NoneType=None, srcmap:tuple=(), data:tuple=(),
    audience:str='', no_code:bool=False, asks:str='', owner:str='', near:bool=True
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

Plan a path (a walk with no source) to goal, make the concepts that the shelf does not have, and save it. srcmap, data, audience, no_code and asks go to the planner. owner goes to it as an instruction of the owner (owner_says). With no_code, no step is a notebook and no new concept has the code way. near=False shows the planner no concepts of the shelf (near_goal), so a walk from given sources gets no idea from other content of the vault.

Walks

A walk from a source has mode='walk'. It is the reading path: one step for each idea, in reading order. Each step has the passage to read (read) and the check to do (check).

_check picks the check of one concept. It uses the stats and the profile of the learner, as Tutor.ask_on does. abhyasa runs no code: when the chosen way is code, the check kind is notebook, and the step runs in Leela. On a tool walk (tool=True), or for a step that needs a library, its reason says so. A step that the plan marks hands='notebook' gets it too.

short_check gives a short-answer check in a text way. A walk uses it when a demo or an order check has no card. The way comes from the text ways of the concept, or from all text ways. A code way is not in the list, because its check is a code task.

source

short_check

def short_check(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, c
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

A short-answer check for concept c, in one of its text ways, or in any text way.

A concept with a demo way and a code way gets a short check in another text way.

from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
ckl = temp_learning()
ck = short_check(ckl, AttrDict(slug='x', name='X', ways=['demo', 'code']))
assert ck.kind == 'short' and ck.way in SHORT_WAYS and ck.depth == 3

A walk has a most number of steps

A long source, such as a docs site, can have 60 ideas or more. A walk of that length is too long to finish, and each step costs model calls for its note and its check. So a walk has at most val('walks.steps') steps (7 by default, and 7 at most; you can change it on the Settings page). A walk from a paper, a book or a page gets a walk map (walk_map, the prompt walk.map): the claim of the source, and 3 to 7 big ideas that a novice must understand to explain it. Each big idea has its understanding, an essential question and its common wrong ideas. The steps are the big ideas. Each other idea is a detail of one big idea: it stays on the step as reading and in Words to know, with no check of its own. A number, a score, a year, an ablation or a remark of the author is never a big idea. When the map fails, main_steps asks the model to pick the main ideas, with the prompt walk.pick. A walk from one of your notebooks gets no map: its ideas are its sections. When the reply has fewer valid numbers, the first ideas that are not picked fill the walk in source order. The steps keep the order of the source, and a prerequisite that is picked comes before the idea that needs it. The pick happens when the walk is made, before any step writes a note or a check. The other ideas stay on the shelf as concepts. The walk keeps their slugs in more, so the plan can say how many more ideas the source has.

pick_prompt

The prompt that asks for the most main ideas of the concepts cs, numbered from 1 in the order of the source.

source

walk_map

def walk_map(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, steps:list, most:int=None, audience:str=''
)->tuple:

(steps, more, map) for the steps of a source: the big ideas of the map, in source order, each with its essential question and its details, the slugs of the other steps, and the map (claim and ideas). Each big idea saves its core and its wrong ideas on its concept. With fewer than 3 steps there is no map. When the reply has no valid idea, main_steps picks the steps and the map is None. audience goes to the map prompt.

source

map_prompt

def map_prompt(
    cs, most:int, audience:str=''
)->str:

The prompt that asks for the claim and the most big ideas of the concepts cs, numbered from 1 in the order of the source. A detail is marked. audience says who the walk is for; it goes in a <source> marker, as data and not as instructions.

The map keeps the big ideas in source order. Each one saves its core and its wrong ideas, and the step keeps its essential question and its details. A score is a detail of the idea that it supports.

from abhyasa.models import Fake
ml = temp_learning()
for n, st in [('Attention', 'Each word weighs every word.'), ('Multi-head attention', 'Several attention heads run side by side.'),
              ('BLEU results', 'The big model reached 28.4 BLEU.'), ('Positional encoding', 'Sines give each position a code.')]: ml.put(n, st, 'ml')
mst = [dict(slug=s) for s in ('attention', 'multi-head-attention', 'bleu-results', 'positional-encoding')]
mfk = Fake({'Return JSON: {"claim"': dict(claim='Attention alone can translate well.', ideas=[
    dict(n=4, understanding='You understand that position codes tell attention the order, because attention alone ignores order.', question='How does the model know word order?', wrong=['attention reads words in order']),
    dict(n=1, understanding='Each word builds its new vector from all words, because it weighs them by match.', question='Why can attention look at all words at once?', details=[3, 1, 2])])})
ss, more, mp = walk_map(ml, mfk, mst)
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in ss], ['attention', 'positional-encoding'])
test_eq((ss[0]['details'], ss[0]['question'], more), (['bleu-results', 'multi-head-attention'], 'Why can attention look at all words at once?', ['multi-head-attention', 'bleu-results']))
test_eq(ml.concept('positional-encoding').core, 'position codes tell attention the order, because attention alone ignores order.')
test_eq(ml.concept('positional-encoding').wrong, [dict(think='attention reads words in order', fact='')])
test_eq(mp['claim'], 'Attention alone can translate well.')

A reply with no valid idea falls back to main_steps, and there is no map. Two steps get no map and no call.

ss, more, mp = walk_map(ml, Fake(), mst, most=3)
test_eq((len(ss), mp), (3, None))
n = Fake(); test_eq(walk_map(ml, n, mst[:2]), (mst[:2], [], None)); test_eq(n.calls, [])

A demo, an order check or a code task takes longer than a short answer. So at most a share of the steps of a walk get one (the setting walks.hands, a third by default, rounded down, and at least 1 in a walk of 3 steps or more). cap_hands counts the hands-on checks in walk order, after main_steps. When the walk has its share, each later step gets a check in its text ways. The count does not depend on chance, so a test can check it. A step that the plan marks hands='notebook' builds part of the goal, so cap_hands leaves it as it is. hands_count counts it apart. The share only warns: the walk editor shows the counts, and nothing stops a walk with more.

source

hands_count

(hands-on checks, steps not skipped, notebooks that build the goal) of steps. A notebook that builds the goal is not a hands-on check. A skipped step does not count.

cap_hands

steps with at most hands_most hands-on checks, the first ones in walk order. Each later step gets a check in its text ways. A step that the plan marks hands='notebook' builds the goal: it stays as it is, and it does not count.

hands_most

def hands_most(
    n:int
)->int:

The most hands-on checks in a walk of n steps: the share walks.hands of them, rounded down, and at least 1 from 3 steps when the share is not 0.

journey_from_source extracts the ideas of one document, and makes one step for each idea of that document, in the order of the document. A step has the passage that extract kept. A concept that you know at depth 4 or more has the status known. A document that is one of your notebooks is not read by the model: notebook_walk (below) uses the notebook as it is.

source

journey_from_source

def journey_from_source(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, ref:str, shelf:str='store', subject:str='', tool:bool=False
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

Make a walk from one vault document, by doc id, source or title. A notebook of yours becomes a notebook_walk. tool marks a library or a command-line tool.

journey_from_text does the same for pasted text. A passage shows only when its quote is in the text word for word.

source

journey_from_text

def journey_from_text(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, text:str, title:str, subject:str='', tool:bool=False
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

Make a walk from pasted text.

A walk from one of your notebooks

A notebook that you wrote is already a lesson, so the walk uses it as it is. nb_file finds the notebook file of a vault document. nb_sections splits the notebook at the headings of its section level (the title at the top is not a section). notebook_walk makes one idea for each section, named by its heading. The passage of the idea is the words and the code of the section, word for word (nb_text), with its source line, so the trust rules of the walk stay: real, verbatim and linked. The statement of the idea is the first sentence of the section. The tutor adds only the check of each idea: a demo where the code of the section draws a picture, else a check in the ways of the idea. The walk keeps the path of the notebook in notebook. With three sections or more, one model call, the walk map (walk_map), keeps the sections that teach a big idea, with the key question of each and the main idea of the notebook. A setup section, as the imports, leaves the plan but stays in the notebook. When the map gives nothing, each section stays.

source

notebook_walk

def notebook_walk(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, d, shelf:str, path:str, subject:str='', tool:bool=False, ask:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

A walk from one of your notebooks, used as it is: one idea for each section, named by its heading. The passage of the idea is the words and the code of the section, word for word, with its source. The tutor adds only the check of each idea: a demo where the code of the section draws a picture, else a check in the ways of the idea, with the share of hands-on checks (cap_hands) for these. With ask and three sections or more, the walk map keeps the sections that teach a big idea (one model call); a setup section stays in the notebook only.

source

nb_text

def nb_text(
    cells
)->str:

The words and the code of cells as one markdown text, word for word: each markdown cell as it is, each code cell in a ``python block, up toNB_SECTION_MOST` characters of whole cells.

source

nb_sections

def nb_sections(
    cells
)->list:

The sections of a notebook with the cells cells, in order, as AttrDict(head, first, last) (the places of its first and last cell). A markdown cell that starts with a heading of the section level starts a section. The section level is the top level of the headings after the title (one # heading at the top). The cells before the first section are not a section.

source

nb_file

def nb_file(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, doc_id:str, shelf:str='store'
)->tuple | None:

(shelf, path) of the notebook file of vault document doc_id, when the document is a notebook that is on this Mac; else None.

A notebook with a title, two sections and a subsection. The subsection is in its section, and the cells before the first section are not one.

from fastcore.nbio import new_nb, mk_cell, write_nb
nbd = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'nbs'; nbd.mkdir()
NB_CELLS = [mk_cell('# DDPM\n\n> Denoising diffusion, from scratch', 'markdown'), mk_cell('import torch'),
            mk_cell('## Introduction', 'markdown'), mk_cell('The 2020 paper made some crucial assumptions that simplify the training of the model. Later models build on it.', 'markdown'),
            mk_cell('## Data loading', 'markdown'), mk_cell('We load Fashion MNIST, and we do not use its labels for this task.', 'markdown'), mk_cell('dls = get_dls()'),
            mk_cell('### Noise schedule', 'markdown'), mk_cell('The noise grows at each step of the forward process.', 'markdown'), mk_cell('show_images(noised)')]
nbp = nbd/'15_DDPM.ipynb'; write_nb(new_nb(NB_CELLS), nbp)
secs = nb_sections(read_nb(nbp).cells)
test_eq([(s.head, s.first, s.last) for s in secs], [('Introduction', 2, 3), ('Data loading', 4, 9)])
t = nb_text(read_nb(nbp).cells[4:10])
assert t.startswith('## Data loading') and '```python\ndls = get_dls()\n```' in t and '### Noise schedule' in t

The notebook goes on a notebook shelf, as Start files it. The walk has one idea for each section, in the words and the code of the notebook, and no model call. The section whose code draws gets a demo check.

from abhyasa.sources import index_notebooks
from abhyasa.models import Fake
nl, nf = temp_learning(), Fake({})
index_notebooks(nl.vault, [nbd])
nd = first(nl.doc_shelf('notebooks').t.docs())
nw = journey_from_source(nl, nf, nd['id'], 'notebooks')
test_eq(nf.calls, [])   # no model call: the notebook is used as it is
test_eq([nl.concept(s['slug']).name for s in nw.steps], ['Introduction', 'Data loading'])
test_eq(Path(nw.notebook['path']).resolve(), nbp.resolve())
r0, r1 = nw.steps[0]['read'], nw.steps[1]['read']
assert r0['text'].startswith('## Introduction') and r0['section'] == 'Introduction' and r0['doc_id'] == nd['id'] and r0['cells'] == [2, 3]
assert 'dls = get_dls()' in r1['text']
test_eq((nw.steps[1]['check']['kind'], nw.steps[1]['check']['why']), ('demo', NB_WHY_DEMO))   # its code draws a picture
test_eq(nl.concept(nw.steps[0]['slug']).statement, 'The 2020 paper made some crucial assumptions that simplify the training of the model.')

With three sections or more, the walk map keeps the sections that teach a big idea. The imports leave the plan, each idea gets its key question, and the walk keeps the main idea.

nbp4 = nbd/'16_DDPM_v2.ipynb'
write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('# DDPM again', 'markdown'), mk_cell('## Imports', 'markdown'), mk_cell("We'll start with some imports.", 'markdown'), mk_cell('import torch'),
                 mk_cell('## Noise', 'markdown'), mk_cell('The forward process adds a little noise at each step, so the last step is pure noise.', 'markdown'),
                 mk_cell('## Model', 'markdown'), mk_cell('A U-Net learns to predict the noise that was added to an image.', 'markdown'),
                 mk_cell('## Sampling', 'markdown'), mk_cell('We start from noise and take away the predicted noise, step by step.', 'markdown')]), nbp4)
index_notebooks(nl.vault, [nbd])
d4 = first(r for r in nl.doc_shelf('notebooks').t.docs() if '16_DDPM_v2' in r['meta'])
ideas = [dict(n=n, understanding=f'Idea {n} does this because of that.', question=q, wrong=[], details=[]) for n, q in ((2, 'Why does the noise grow?'), (3, 'What does the model predict?'), (4, 'How does a picture come out of noise?'))]
mf = Fake({'Ideas, in the order of the source': dict(claim='A model that learns to remove noise can make new pictures from noise.', ideas=ideas)})
mw = journey_from_source(nl, mf, d4['id'], 'notebooks')
test_eq(len(mf.calls), 1)
test_eq([nl.concept(s['slug']).name for s in mw.steps], ['Noise', 'Model', 'Sampling'])   # Imports teaches no idea of the notebook
test_eq([s['question'] for s in mw.steps], [x['question'] for x in ideas])
test_eq((mw.map['claim'], [nl.concept(s).name for s in mw.more]), ('A model that learns to remove noise can make new pictures from noise.', ['Imports']))
test_eq([s['read']['cells'] for s in mw.steps], [[4, 5], [6, 7], [8, 9]])   # each idea keeps its cells, so Leela opens at its section

The learner learns the notebook in Leela. learning_copy writes a learning copy for Leela in the folder of the walk (copy_path, in the vault assets): the notebook as it is, with the demo of each idea as a ```rupaka block in a markdown cell after its section. Leela draws the block. The learner’s own notebook is only read. A copy at the path of the notebook itself is refused.

source

learning_copy

def learning_copy(
    j, dest, demos:NoneType=None
)->pathlib.Path:

Write the learning copy of the notebook of walk j to dest: the notebook as it is, with the demo of each idea (demos maps a slug to a rupaka spec) as a markdown cell with a ``rupaka block after the last cell of its section. Leela draws the block. The learner's own notebook is only read, never written. Returndest`.

source

copy_path

def copy_path(
    assets, j
)->pathlib.Path:

The path of the learning copy of the notebook of walk j: <assets>/walks/<walk id>/<name of the notebook>, in the folder of the walk.

The copy has one more cell, the demo, after the last cell of its section. The notebook file has the same bytes as before.

spec = dict(id='noise-demo', title='Noise', state={}, blocks=[])
dest = copy_path(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'assets', nw)
test_eq((dest.parent.name, dest.parent.parent.name, dest.name), (nw.id, 'walks', '15_DDPM.ipynb'))
was = nbp.read_bytes()
learning_copy(nw, dest, {nw.steps[1]['slug']: spec})
cp = read_nb(dest)
test_eq(len(cp.cells), len(NB_CELLS) + 1)
assert cp.cells[10].source.startswith('**A demo: Data loading.**') and '```rupaka' in cp.cells[10].source and '"noise-demo"' in cp.cells[10].source
test_eq(nbp.read_bytes(), was)   # your own notebook does not change
test_fail(lambda: learning_copy(nw, nbp, {}), contains='your own notebook')

journey_from_sources makes one walk across many pages, for example the pages of a docs site that file_link filed. The tutor reads each page in turn. The steps come in page order, and in each page in the order of the page. An idea that two pages name gets one step, in the first page where its passage is. When no page has its passage, the step is in the first page that names it. progress(k, n) hears of page k of n before the tutor reads it.

source

journey_from_sources

def journey_from_sources(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, docs:list, title:str='', subject:str='', progress:NoneType=None,
    tool:bool=False, audience:str='', no_code:bool=False, **extra
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

Make one walk across the vault documents docs, each with shelf, doc_id, title and url, in their order. extra goes on the walk. audience (who the walk is for) goes to the walk map; with no_code, no check is code. The walk keeps both.

walk_from_topic plans a path to the goal. With the chips of the Start box, the planner sees the source map and the data list, and each step reads the paragraph of its doc that names the most main words of the idea, and at least half of them. A step with no doc reads the first passage in your sources that names the idea or an alias. A passage from a source that the goal named may instead name every main word of the idea. A weak match is no source: the step has no read, the page shows the tutor’s words, and research can look on the web.

Your data

A course or a walk can keep folders of your own data in data, as a list of {path, note}, or {path, note, name} when you gave the folder the data name of a step. abhyasa does not file these folders and does not learn from them. The exercises run on them in Leela. data_row checks one folder, and keep_data adds it to a list. data_entries makes the data entries of a notebook spec: the name of the row, else an upper-case name from the folder name, the path, and what, with the note and a short listing of the folder. A row with no name (an older row) still works: it gets a name from its folder.

with_data puts the entries of a step on these folders. The folders of the walk (a course gives its folders to each of its walks) are the one set of data names. An entry never keeps a path that the model wrote: an entry with the name or the path of a folder gets the name and path of that folder, and any other entry keeps its name and what with no path and need: true. That is a folder that the learner must add under Your data.

source

with_data

def with_data(
    entries, rows
)->list:

The data entries entries on your data folders rows only, then an entry for each folder that they do not name, at most DATA_MOST in all. An entry with the name or the path of a folder gets that folder. Any other entry has no path and need: the learner adds its folder.

source

data_entries

def data_entries(
    rows, taken:tuple=()
)->list:

The data folders rows as data entries {name, path, what, need} of a notebook spec. A row with a name keeps it. Each other name is new: not in taken, and not used twice.

source

with_stop

def with_stop(
    s
)->str:

s as one line that ends with a stop: a text that ends with ., ! or ? gets no second stop. ’’ stays ’’.

source

folder_list

def folder_list(
    path, most:int=10
)->str:

The names of the first most entries of folder path that do not start with a dot, and how many more. ’’ when abhyasa cannot read it.

source

keep_data

def keep_data(
    rows, path, note:str='', name:str=''
)->list:

rows with the data folder path, its note and its data name at the end, one time for each path and each name. A ValueError says why abhyasa cannot add it.

source

data_row

def data_row(
    path, note:str='', name:str=''
)->dict:

The data folder path as a row {path, note} (and name, when given), with ~ for the home folder. A ValueError says in one line why abhyasa cannot use it.

A folder in your home folder is a data row, with ~ and its note. A path outside the home folder, a path that is not a folder, and a ninth folder are refused, each with one plain line. Here the home folder is a temporary folder.

home, old = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve(), os.environ['HOME']
os.environ['HOME'] = str(home)
try:
    (eps := home/'ramayana-episodes').mkdir(); (eps/'episodes.json').write_text('{}'); (eps/'characters.json').write_text('[]'); (eps/'.hidden').write_text('')
    rows = keep_data([], str(eps), 'The 418 episodes:\nmy scenarios run on them.')
    test_eq(rows, [dict(path='~/ramayana-episodes', note='The 418 episodes: my scenarios run on them.')])
    test_eq(keep_data(rows, '~/ramayana-episodes', 'New note.'), [dict(path='~/ramayana-episodes', note='New note.')])   # one row for each path
    for bad, said in (('/etc', 'not in your home folder'), (str(eps/'episodes.json'), 'no folder'), ('~/nothing', 'no folder')):
        with ExceptionExpected(ValueError, said): keep_data(rows, bad)
    with ExceptionExpected(ValueError, 'at most 8'): keep_data([dict(path=f'~/d{k}', note='') for k in range(8)], str(eps))
    es = data_entries(rows)
finally: os.environ['HOME'] = old
test_eq(es, [dict(name='RAMAYANA_EPISODES', path='~/ramayana-episodes', what='The 418 episodes: my scenarios run on them. It holds: characters.json, episodes.json.', need=False)])

A name that a step uses already gets a number. with_data keeps the entries of the step first, and adds only the folders that they do not name. An entry on a folder gets the name of the folder. Each entry passes the check of a notebook spec.

from abhyasa.contract import validate_nb_spec, _GOOD
test_eq([e['name'] for e in data_entries([dict(path='~/x/2024 data', note=''), dict(path='~/y/2024-data', note='')], taken=['D_2024_DATA'])], ['D_2024_DATA_2', 'D_2024_DATA_3'])
step = [dict(name='IMAGES', path='~/Pictures/comic', what='your images', need=True)]
test_eq([e['name'] for e in with_data(step, [dict(path='~/Pictures/comic', note=''), dict(path='~/ramayana-episodes', note='')])], ['COMIC', 'RAMAYANA_EPISODES'])
test_eq(validate_nb_spec({**_GOOD, 'data': es})['data'], es)

A row with a name keeps that name, also when a folder without a name would take it. A note that ends with a stop gets no second stop:

rows = [dict(path='~/x/episodes', note=''), dict(path='~/y/comics', note='The text of the comic episodes.', name='EPISODES')]
test_eq([(e['name'], e['what']) for e in data_entries(rows)], [('EPISODES_2', 'Your data folder.'), ('EPISODES', 'The text of the comic episodes.')])
test_eq((with_stop('Text of the episodes'), with_stop('Text of the episodes.'), with_stop('Why?'), with_stop('')), ('Text of the episodes.', 'Text of the episodes.', 'Why?', ''))

With no folders, a path that the model wrote goes, and the entry keeps its name and what. The learner adds that folder.

invented = [dict(name='EPISODES', path='~/comics/episodes.txt', what='the text of your comic episodes', need=False), dict(name='IMAGES', path='~/comic_images', what='your images', need=False)]
test_eq(with_data(invented, None), [dict(name='EPISODES', path='', what='the text of your comic episodes', need=True), dict(name='IMAGES', path='', what='your images', need=True)])
test_eq(validate_nb_spec({**_GOOD, 'data': with_data(invented, [])})['data'][0]['path'], '')

With a folder of that name, the entry gets its path. A second entry on the same folder goes.

test_eq([(e['name'], e['path'], e['need']) for e in with_data([*invented, {**invented[0], 'what': ''}], [dict(path='~/x/episodes', note='')])],
        [('EPISODES', '~/x/episodes', False), ('IMAGES', '', True)])

Across a walk, one folder has one name. walk_names gives the data names that the other steps of the walk use. same_names gives an entry the name that the walk uses for the same what, also in the text of the spec.

source

same_names

def same_names(
    spec, named
)->dict:

Notebook spec spec with each data entry whose what is the what of an entry in named (the walk names it) under the name of that entry. The name changes in the task, the stub and the run too, so they name the same data.

source

walk_names

def walk_names(
    j, i:int | None=None
)->list:

The data entries {name, what} that the notebook specs of the steps of walk j (not step i) name: the first entry for each name and for each what.

Steps 1 and 2 name the same images, so the walk keeps only the first name, IMAGES:

eps = dict(name='EPISODES', what='Text file of the comic episodes.')
j2 = AttrDict(steps=[dict(nb=dict(data=[eps, dict(name='IMAGES', what='The comic images.')])), dict(nb=dict(data=[dict(name='COMIC_IMAGES', what='the comic images')])), dict()])
test_eq(walk_names(j2, 1), [eps, dict(name='IMAGES', what='The comic images.')])
test_eq([d['name'] for d in walk_names(j2)], ['EPISODES', 'IMAGES'])   # the second name for the same images is not a new name

A new spec that calls the images COMIC_IMAGES gets IMAGES. A longer name that starts the same way stays as it is:

mine = dict(task='Load COMIC_IMAGES.', stub='def f(): pass', data=[dict(name='COMIC_IMAGES', path='', what='The comic images', need=True)],
            run=dict(say='Write the run here: read COMIC_IMAGES and COMIC_IMAGES_2.', predict=''))
got = same_names(mine, walk_names(j2))
test_eq((got['task'], got['data'][0]['name'], got['run']['say']), ('Load IMAGES.', 'IMAGES', 'Write the run here: read IMAGES and COMIC_IMAGES_2.'))
assert same_names(mine, []) is mine

The data that a walk still needs

missing_data gives the data entries {name, what} that the notebook steps of a walk name and that have no folder under Your data. With i, it looks only at step i. The page asks for each one with one short line: data_line keeps the first sentence of what (short_what), with no second stop.

source

missing_data

def missing_data(
    j, i:int | None=None
)->list:

The data entries {name, what} that the notebook specs of walk j (or of step i only) name, and that no folder under Your data (j.data) has.

source

data_line

def data_line(
    d
)->str:

The line for data entry d that has no folder: EPISODES: the text of the comic episodes. The page puts the action (Set it) after it.

source

short_what

def short_what(
    w, most:int=80
)->str:

The first sentence of w, at most about most characters, with no stop at its end and no “folder of” at its start, to go after a name and a colon. Each word keeps its case. Only a first word that is a common word (COMMON, or a word before “of”) gets a small letter, so “Indian” stays.

The line has the name, a short form of what and one stop, and no action: the page adds Set it. A long what is cut at a word:

test_eq(data_line(dict(name='EPISODES', what='Text of the comic episodes. Short caption lines are taken from it and used as prompts.')),
        'EPISODES: the text of the comic episodes.')
test_eq(data_line(dict(name='IMAGES', what='Folder of your own Indian comic panel images. Name the folder you want to use.')),
        'IMAGES: your own Indian comic panel images.')
test_eq(data_line(dict(name='RAMAYANA', what='')), 'The folder of RAMAYANA.')
long = short_what('A very long description of the images ' * 4)
assert len(long) <= 81 and long.startswith('a very') and long.endswith('…') and '..' not in long

A word with a capital keeps it. Only a common first word, as “The” or “A”, gets a small letter:

test_eq(short_what('Indian comic page or panel images (jpg or png) that you choose and name.'), 'Indian comic page or panel images (jpg or png) that you choose and name')
test_eq(short_what('Ramayana episodes as JSON.'), 'Ramayana episodes as JSON')
test_eq([short_what(x) for x in ('The comic images.', 'A list of names.', 'PNG panels.')], ['the comic images', 'a list of names', 'PNG panels'])

Step 0 names EPISODES and IMAGES. With a folder named EPISODES under Your data, only IMAGES is missing. Step 2 has no notebook:

j3 = AttrDict(steps=[dict(nb=dict(data=[eps, dict(name='IMAGES', what='The comic images.')])), dict(nb=dict(data=[dict(name='IMAGES', what='the comic images')])), dict()], data=[])
test_eq([d['name'] for d in missing_data(j3)], ['EPISODES', 'IMAGES'])
test_eq([d['name'] for d in missing_data({**j3, 'data': [dict(path='~/comics', note='', name='EPISODES')]})], ['IMAGES'])
test_eq(missing_data(j3, 2), [])

source

walk_from_topic

def walk_from_topic(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, goal:str, who:str='', sources:NoneType=None, tool:bool=False, chips:tuple=(),
    data:tuple=(), audience:str='', no_code:bool=False, asks:str='', owner:str='', near:bool=True
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

Plan a path to goal and make it a walk of at most walks.steps steps, with a passage and a check on each step. With chips (the chip ids of the Start box), the planner sees the source_map. With data (your data folders, {path, note}), the planner sees their data entries, and the walk keeps them. audience (who the walk is for) and no_code go to the planner and stay on the walk; asks (what you ask for this plan) goes only to the planner, and so does owner, as an instruction of the owner (owner_says).

minutes guesses the time for one step: reading at 200 words a minute, plus the time of its check.

source

minutes

def minutes(
    step
)->int:

The minutes for one step: its passage at 200 words a minute, plus the time of its check.

Rabbit holes

A step can need an idea that you have not learned. For example, the scaling by √dk in a paper on attention needs gradients. These functions find what is missing, make a short side walk on it, and link the side walk back to the step.

needs lists the prereqs of a concept, then its gaps. A need is met at depth READY (3) or more, as in model.ready.

source

needs

def needs(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, slug:str, by:dict=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:

The prereqs, then the gaps, of concept slug that are on the shelf. ok is true at depth READY or more.

walk_needs gives each need of a step a state by the same count as the walk (walk_state). A need that is a step of this walk that you closed solid is done, with at, its index. A need that you closed shaky is shaky. Else a need in met (a side walk today) is today, also when its side check made it ready, a need at depth READY is learned, and the rest is missing. So the line never says “not learned yet” for an idea that the walk just did.

source

walk_needs

def walk_needs(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, j, i:int, by:dict=None, met:tuple=()
)->fastcore.foundation.L:

The needs of step i of walk j (needs), each with state: done, shaky, learned, today or missing, and at, the index of the step that did it.

known_how says how you know one idea at a step, by the same rule, for a gap that your answer showed. A side walk from this step that ended solid or fragile is side. Then the steps of this walk count (done, shaky), then a side walk that ended shaky, then the depth on the shelf (learned). Else the idea is missing.

source

known_how

def known_how(
    j, i:int, slug:str, by:dict
)->tuple:

How you know concept slug at step i of walk j: (state, index), with state side, done, shaky, learned or missing, and the index of the step that did it.

pick_way_down picks how to learn a missing idea:

  • primer: one step and one short check. You met the idea before (depth 1 or 2), or it needs no other idea that you have not learned.
  • walk: a side walk on the chain, at most walks.chain (4 by default) ideas. The chain is the unready prereqs, deepest first, then the idea.
  • course: a big topic. The gap is more than walks.chain ideas on the shelf, or the tutor said that the idea builds on COURSE_AT (6) ideas or more when it added it (size). It opens as its own course, with a level check and stages.

The size of the gap picks the depth. The learner can always pick one of the other two.

source

pick_way_down

def pick_way_down(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, slug:str, by:dict=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

How to learn concept slug before you go on: a quick primer, a side walk, or its own course, with why in one line. The gap is the unready prereqs on the shelf, or the size that the tutor gave, the larger of the two.

source

gap_size

def gap_size(
    c
)->int:

The number of ideas that concept c builds on, as the tutor said when it added it (size), from 0 to 20.

detour makes the side walk and starts it. It keeps parent (the walk and the step that opened it) and depth. A side walk of a side walk has depth 2. Past walks.depth (2 by default), only its own session can open, at depth 0. With no chain on the shelf, the side walk is a short path that plan makes, with steps as walk_from_topic makes them. The planned walk is not kept. It always ends on the idea.

source

detour

def detour(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, slug:str, parent:dict, how:str='walk', sources:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

Make and start a side walk on concept slug, as a child of parent ({walk, step}, or a place in Leela).

parent_step gives the walk and the step that opened side walk j, when both are still there. Else it gives (None, None). The walk page, the side pane, the history and the walk list use it, so they agree on “the parent step is still there”. With js, a dictionary of walks by id, it reads no walk from the shelf.

source

parent_step

def parent_step(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, j, js:dict=None
)->tuple:

The parent walk and step of side walk j, when the walk is there and has that step (found by its concept); else (None, None). js maps ids to walks that are already read.

source

parent_at

def parent_at(
    pj, p
)->int | None:

The place now, in walk pj, of the step that the parent p of a side walk names: by its concept (idea) when it has one, else by its place step.

trail gives the walks from the root walk down to a side walk, for the crumbs. back_from keeps the result of a side walk on the step that opened it, in detours. The result is the outcome of the last step, or skipped. One side walk has one record. When you come back again with a new outcome, the record changes, and at is the time of the new outcome. A later skip does not change a record.

source

back_from

def back_from(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, jid:str
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:

Keep the result of side walk jid on the step that opened it: one record for each side walk, updated when its outcome changes. Return the parent walk, or None.

source

trail

def trail(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, jid:str
)->fastcore.foundation.L:

The walks from the root walk to walk jid, each with the step that you are on.

for_talk tells a walk that is for the room: a side walk that a talk opened (its parent is {talk, slide}), or the walk that a talk was made from, from a path, a walk with no source (its parent is {journey, for: 'talk'}). Such a walk is not your own learning, so the pages that list your walks and the steps you read skip it.

source

for_talk

def for_talk(
    j
)->bool:

Whether walk j is for a talk: a side walk that a talk opened beside a slide, or the walk that a talk was made from, from a path.

A walk with a talk parent, or one made for a talk from a path, is for the room. A walk with a walk parent, or with no parent, is your own.

assert for_talk(dict(parent={'talk': 't-1', 'slide': 's3'})) and not for_talk(dict(parent={'walk': 'w-1', 'step': 0}))
assert for_talk(dict(parent={'journey': 'j-1', 'for': 'talk'})) and not for_talk(dict(parent={'journey': 'j-1'}))
assert not for_talk({}) and not for_talk(None) and not for_talk(dict(parent=None))

A talk from your sources has a hidden walk under it, so the talk builder and each rebuild read src.walk as before. file_chip files the source of one chip of the Start box, or finds the documents of a chip that is in the vault. walk_for_talk files the chips and makes the walk, with parent={'for': 'talk'}, so for_talk hides it. With a goal, it is a goal walk, as Start makes it. With no goal and one notebook as the only source, it is one step for each section of the notebook, in order (notebook_walk with no walk map), so no idea is renamed or moved. Else it is one walk across the documents. The walk keeps audience and no_code.

source

walk_for_talk

def walk_for_talk(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, chips, goal:str='', audience:str='', no_code:bool=False, sources:NoneType=None,
    said:function=noop, owner:str='', near:bool=True
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

File the chips chips, and make and save the hidden walk of a talk from them. said gets each stage. The walk of one notebook takes the title of the notebook (nb_title). owner (what the owner asks for, such as the roles of the sources) goes to the planner (owner_says), and the walk keeps it as its change, so the slide writer gets it too.

source

nb_title

def nb_title(
    path
)->str:

The title of the notebook at path: its first # heading, else its file name in words (02_agentic_engineering.ipynb gives Agentic engineering).

source

file_chip

def file_chip(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, i:str
)->fastcore.foundation.L:

The documents of the chip id i: it files a gh:, folder:, repo:, file: or link: source, and finds a vault: or doc: one.

A notebook with three sections, under a home folder for the test, gives a hidden walk with one step for each section, in order, and no model call. The walk takes the first # heading of the notebook as its title, not the name of its vault document. These tests need their own imports.

import os, tempfile
from fastcore.nbio import new_nb, mk_cell, write_nb
from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
from abhyasa.models import Fake
twh, twold = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve(), os.environ['HOME']
os.environ['HOME'] = str(twh)
try:
    twp = twh/'talks'/'agents.ipynb'; twp.parent.mkdir()
    write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('# Agents', 'markdown'), mk_cell('## Tool calls', 'markdown'), mk_cell('The model names a tool, and the agent runs it.', 'markdown'),
                     mk_cell('## The agent loop', 'markdown'), mk_cell('print(2 + 3)'), mk_cell('## Memory between turns', 'markdown')]), twp)
    twl, twf = temp_learning(), Fake({})
    tww = walk_for_talk(twl, twf, [f'file:{twp}'], audience='Engineers who are new to agents', no_code=True)
finally: os.environ['HOME'] = twold
test_eq([twl.concept(s['slug']).name for s in tww.steps], ['Tool calls', 'The agent loop', 'Memory between turns'])
assert for_talk(tww) and twf.calls == [] and tww.chips == [f'file:{twp}'] and tww.title == 'Agents'
(tww.audience, tww.no_code, tww.notebook['path'] == str(twp))

A notebook with no # heading takes its file name in words, with no number at its start.

ntp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'02_agentic_engineering.ipynb'
write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('## Tool calls', 'markdown')]), ntp)
test_eq(nb_title(ntp), 'Agentic engineering')

walk_from_talk makes a walk of your own from the hidden walk of a talk. You use it after a talk on a topic, to learn the topic yourself. The new walk has the steps of the hidden walk in the order of the slides, and no parent, so it shows on Home. The talk gives the order, because this module does not read talks. A step that is not in the order is left out. The new walk keeps the notebook, the sources and who it is for, and none of the progress of the hidden walk.

source

walk_from_talk

def walk_from_talk(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, jid:str, order
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

Make and save a walk of your own from the hidden walk jid of a talk: its steps in the order of the concept slugs order (the slides), with no parent and no progress.

A hidden walk with three steps, and a talk with two of them in another order, gives a walk with those two steps in the talk order. It has no parent, so it is not for a talk, and no step keeps its progress.

wl = temp_learning()
hw = wl.put_journey(dict(id='agents-h1', title='Agents', goal='Read Agents', mode='walk', parent={'for': 'talk'}, chips=['file:/u/k/a.ipynb'], notebook=dict(path='/u/k/a.ipynb'),
                         steps=[dict(slug='loop', status='todo', done=dict(outcome='right')), dict(slug='tools', status='todo'), dict(slug='memory', status='todo')]))
mine = walk_from_talk(wl, hw.id, ['memory', 'loop'])
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in mine.steps], ['memory', 'loop'])
test_eq((mine.get('parent'), for_talk(mine), mine.notebook, mine.chips), (None, False, dict(path='/u/k/a.ipynb'), ['file:/u/k/a.ipynb']))
assert mine.id != hw.id and not any('done' in s for s in mine.steps)
test_fail(lambda: walk_from_talk(wl, hw.id, ['gone']), contains='no idea')

The place that you used last

last_place says where Continue goes. It is the one function for the top bar, the card on Today and the card of a course. A place is a step of a walk that is not finished, or an open session with no walk. Each walk gives the time that you used it last: the idea that you were on (here, which the idea page writes), the newest idea that you read, or the start. A session gives the time of its last change. The newest place wins. A side walk counts as the step that opened it, so Continue goes back to the paper. A side walk whose step is not there now (or that Leela opened) is never a place. Only the newest most walks are read. The step is the idea that you were on when it is not done, else the current step of the walk.

source

last_place

def last_place(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, by:dict=None, most:int=10
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:

The place that you used last, or None. A walk place has walk, step, title, done, total and course; a session place has session and title. Each has at, the time that you used it.

source

used_at

def used_at(
    j
)->float:

When you last used walk j: the idea that you were on, the newest idea that you read, or the start; else when it was made.

source

is_open

def is_open(
    s
)->bool:

Whether filed session s is open: it has a log, it did not end, and it has an answer or an open question.

A walk that you read now wins over an older open session, and the session wins when you use it after the walk.

pl2 = temp_learning(); pl2.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml'); pl2.put('Fusion', 'Join two lists.', 'ml')
two = [dict(slug='ranking', status='todo', check={}), dict(slug='fusion', status='todo', check={})]
now = time.time()
pl2.put_journey(dict(id='wa', title='Walk A', mode='walk', steps=two, started=now - 60, here=dict(step=1, at=now - 30)))
pl2.log_session('s1', 'open', start=now - 900, updated=now - 600, focus='ranking', concepts=['ranking'], log=[], open=True)
p = last_place(pl2)
test_eq((p.walk, p.step, p.title, p.done, p.total), ('wa', 1, 'Walk A', 0, 2))
pl2.log_session('s1', 'open', start=now - 900, updated=now, focus='ranking', concepts=['ranking'], log=[], open=True)
test_eq((last_place(pl2).session, last_place(pl2).title), ('s1', 'Ranking'))

A side walk counts as the step that opened it. A finished walk, a walk for a talk and an ended session are not places.

pl2.log_session('s1', 'open', start=now - 900, updated=now - 900, focus='ranking', concepts=['ranking'], log=[], ended=now - 900)
pl2.put_journey(dict(id='side', title='Side', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug='fusion', status='todo', check={})], parent=dict(walk='wa', step=1, slug='fusion'), here=dict(step=0, at=now)))
test_eq((last_place(pl2).walk, last_place(pl2).step), ('wa', 1))
pl2.put_journey(dict(id='talk', title='Talk', mode='walk', steps=two, parent=dict(talk='t1', slide='s1'), here=dict(step=0, at=now + 9)))
test_eq(last_place(pl2).walk, 'wa')
for x in ('wa', 'side'): pl2.merge_journey(x, steps=[{**s, 'done': dict(outcome='solid', at=now)} for s in pl2.journey(x).steps])
test_eq(last_place(pl2), None)

A side walk with no parent step in a walk here is not a place: its walk is gone, or Leela opened it.

pl3 = temp_learning(); pl3.put('Fusion', 'Join two lists.', 'ml')
one = [dict(slug='fusion', status='todo', check={})]
pl3.put_journey(dict(id='gone', title='Gone', mode='walk', steps=one, parent=dict(walk='nowhere', step=0), here=dict(step=0, at=now)))
pl3.put_journey(dict(id='lee', title='From Leela', mode='walk', steps=one, parent=dict(leela='lesson-1'), here=dict(step=0, at=now)))
test_eq(last_place(pl3), None)

An old path becomes a walk

Before 0.0.16 a goal could give a path: a walk with no mode, no passage and no check of its own. walk_path makes such a path a topic walk, one time, with the same id: the same steps in the same order, each with a check, as walk_from_topic does. A step that you marked known or skipped stays so, and an idea that you learned is known.

The walk keeps the progress of the sessions of the path. A step with answers is done or shaky. The newest open session is the sitting, with its open question, which goes on the shelf of open questions (_keep_open), so the step shows it. started and here come from the sessions, so an old path does not become the newest walk.

walk_path does not search the sources, so it is fast. step_read finds the passage of one step when its idea opens. walk_paths does it for each path, and gives the ids.

source

step_read

def step_read(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, jid:str, slug:str, sources:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:

Find the passage of the step on slug of walk jid that walk_path left for later (read_later), one time, and save it. The walk now, or None when the step needs no search.

source

walk_paths

def walk_paths(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning
)->list:

Make each old path a topic walk (walk_path). The ids of the walks that changed.

source

walk_path

def walk_path(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, j
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:

Path j (an old walk with no mode) as a topic walk with the same id, one time, with the progress of its sessions (_with_runs). A walk stays as it is. No step is searched now: step_read finds the passage of a step when its idea opens.

The tests use a temporary shelf and the Fake model.

from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
from abhyasa.models import Fake

look_up finds a term that you select. A term that is not on the shelf becomes a gap of the step, through name_gaps.

source

look_up

def look_up(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, term:str, at:str='', sources:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:

Find term on the shelf by slug, name or alias. Else add it as a gap of the concept of step at ('<walk id>/<step>').

Name a topic, find the parts of a step

topic_slug finds a topic by name. When the shelf knows the name, topic_slug uses that concept. For a new name, the model writes a short statement.

source

topic_slug

def topic_slug(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, j, name:str, sources:NoneType=None
)->str | None:

The slug of the concept name on the shelf. The tutor writes a new concept when the shelf has none: the name goes in a fence, with no control marks, cut to NAME_MOST. None for a name that is not an idea.

name_gaps keeps each idea that you say you do not know as a gap of the concept you learn. It finds the idea on the shelf by name or alias. Or it adds the idea with a short statement. Next time the gap comes first, but it does not block the concept.

source

name_gaps

def name_gaps(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, slug:str, terms, sources:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:

Find or add a concept for each idea in terms, and keep it as a gap of slug. Return the gap slugs.

A new idea becomes a concept with a statement and the gap provenance. name_gaps finds an idea that is already on the shelf by its alias. It does not add that idea again.

from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
from abhyasa.models import Fake
ngl = temp_learning(); ngl.put('Functions and the neuron', 'z = w . x + b.', 'ml'); ngl.put('Bias', 'A constant added to z.', 'ml', aliases=['the bias'])
gask = Fake({'The idea: the loop': dict(name='Weighted sum as a loop', statement='A loop adds each weight times its input.')})
test_eq(name_gaps(ngl, gask, 'functions-and-the-neuron', ['the loop', 'the bias', 'the loop']), ['weighted-sum-as-a-loop', 'bias'])
g = ngl.concept('weighted-sum-as-a-loop')
test_eq((g.aliases, g.provenance[0]['src'], g.provenance[0]['of']), (['the loop'], 'gap', 'functions-and-the-neuron'))
test_eq(ngl.concept('functions-and-the-neuron').gaps, ['weighted-sum-as-a-loop', 'bias'])

A statement that is not plain is written again one time, in plain English, before it goes on the shelf.

hard = 'This leverages the schedule; the network must facilitate the removal of the noise at each step.'
easy = 'The network removes some noise at each step.'
pask = Fake({'Write this text again': easy, 'The idea: the schedule': dict(name='Noise schedule', statement=hard)})
test_eq(ngl.concept(name_gaps(ngl, pask, 'functions-and-the-neuron', ['the schedule'])[0]).statement, easy)

A big topic gets its size from the tutor. pick_way_down then picks its own course for it, with the reason in one line.

gask.rules['The idea: diffusion'] = dict(name='Diffusion model', statement='A model that learns to undo noise, step by step.', size=8)
d = first(name_gaps(ngl, gask, 'functions-and-the-neuron', ['diffusion']))
test_eq((ngl.concept(d).size, pick_way_down(ngl, d).how, pick_way_down(ngl, d).why), (8, 'course', 'a big topic: 8 ideas that you have not learned yet'))
test_eq(pick_way_down(ngl, 'weighted-sum-as-a-loop').how, 'primer')   # no size and no prereqs: a quick primer

A term such as x makes no concept, and the tutor is not asked about it.

n0 = len(gask.calls)
test_eq(name_gaps(ngl, gask, 'functions-and-the-neuron', ['x', ' ']), [])
test_eq((len(gask.calls), ngl.concept('x')), (n0, None))

split divides a big step into smaller steps. It runs extract over the statement of the step and the passages from the learner’s sources. The concepts that it finds go before the step, as its prereqs.

source

split_parts

def split_parts(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, jid:str, slug:str, sources:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:

Find the parts of step slug of walk jid with the tutor, and keep each as a prereq of slug. Return the slugs that are not steps of the walk. It does not change the walk.

source

Learning.repair_subjects

def repair_subjects()->list:

One time on a vault: give the subject of its walk to each concept of the walk that has none (a walk with no subject uses the most common one of its concepts). The group stays. A concept that you moved by hand stays. Return the slugs that changed.

A concept with no subject gets the subject of its walk

split gives its parts the subject of the step, or else the subject of the walk. _fill_subject gives the subject of a walk to the concepts that it made with none. A concept that you moved by hand stays.

sp = temp_learning(); sp.put('Attention', 'Weights on values.')                       # no subject
sp.put_journey(dict(id='jx', title='T', goal='g', subject='nlp', steps=[dict(slug='attention')], mode='walk', created=0))
spf = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=[dict(name='Query', statement='A vector.')])})
test_eq(split_parts(sp, spf, 'jx', 'attention'), ['query'])
test_eq(sp.concept('query').subject, 'nlp')                                                # the subject of the walk, as the step has none
sp.put('Key', 'A vector.'); sp.put('Pinned', 'Mine.'); sp.set_group('pinned', ['mine'], by='hand')
test_eq(_fill_subject(sp, ['key', 'pinned', 'query'], 'nlp'), 'nlp')
test_eq([sp.concept(s).subject for s in ('key', 'pinned', 'query')], ['nlp', '', 'nlp'])
sp.put('Value', 'A vector.', 'ml')
test_eq(_fill_subject(sp, ['value', 'attention'], ''), 'ml')                              # the most common subject of the walk
test_eq(sp.concept('attention').subject, 'ml')

One repair for old concepts in General

repair_subjects runs one time on a vault. A concept with no subject, in a walk that has a subject, gets that subject. A walk with no subject uses the most common subject of its concepts. The group of a concept stays. A concept that you placed by hand does not move, and the mark says that the repair ran.

rs = temp_learning()
for n in ('Alpha one', 'Beta one', 'Gamma one', 'Pinned one', 'Lone one'): rs.put(n, 'Idea.')
rs.put('Delta one', 'Idea.', 'ml'); rs.put('Eps one', 'Idea.')
rs.set_group('beta-one', ['Bits'], by='model'); rs.set_group('pinned-one', ['Mine'], by='hand')
rs.put_journey(dict(id='j1', title='T1', goal='g', subject='transformers', mode='walk', created=0, more=['gamma-one'],
                    steps=[dict(slug=s) for s in ('alpha-one', 'beta-one', 'pinned-one')]))
rs.put_journey(dict(id='j2', title='T2', goal='g', subject='', mode='walk', created=0, steps=[dict(slug='delta-one'), dict(slug='eps-one')]))
rs.v.forget(first(rs.v.t.docs(where='source=?', where_args=['learning://marker/subjects']))['id'])
test_eq(sorted(rs.repair_subjects()), ['alpha-one', 'beta-one', 'eps-one', 'gamma-one'])
test_eq([rs.concept(s).subject for s in ('alpha-one', 'beta-one', 'gamma-one', 'pinned-one', 'lone-one', 'eps-one')], ['transformers', 'transformers', 'transformers', '', '', 'ml'])
test_eq((rs.concept('beta-one').group, rs.concept('alpha-one').get('group'), rs.concept('pinned-one').group), (['Bits'], None, ['Mine']))
test_eq(rs.repair_subjects(), [])                                                         # one time
rs.put('Zeta one', 'Idea.'); rs.put_journey(dict(id='j3', title='T3', goal='g', subject='nlp', mode='walk', created=0, steps=[dict(slug='zeta-one')]))
test_eq(rs.repair_subjects(), [])                                                         # the mark is set: it does not look again
test_eq(rs.concept('zeta-one').subject, '')

A concept that you kept out of the groups by hand (an empty group) is not moved by the repair, with or without a group name.

hs = temp_learning(); hs.put('Kept one', 'Idea.'); hs.set_group('kept-one', [], by='hand')
hs.put_journey(dict(id='j9', title='T9', goal='g', subject='nlp', mode='walk', created=0, steps=[dict(slug='kept-one')]))
hs.v.forget(first(hs.v.t.docs(where='source=?', where_args=['learning://marker/subjects']))['id'])
test_eq((hs.repair_subjects(), hs.concept('kept-one').subject, hs.concept('kept-one').group_by), ([], '', 'hand'))

Related topics

related gives the concepts next to slug in the graph. First come the concepts that build on it, then the related ones, then its prereqs. The concepts that are not learned come first. with_step finds the walks that have a concept.

source

with_step

def with_step(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, slug:str
)->fastcore.foundation.L:

(walk, index) for each walk that has step slug.

source

related

def related(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, slug:str, k:int=6, goal:int=None, by:dict=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:

Up to k concepts next to slug: what builds on it, what relates to it, then what it needs.

Tests

A fake model plans a path to LLMs. The shelf has attention already, at depth 3.

from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
from abhyasa.models import Fake
lr = temp_learning()
lr.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml')
lr.update('attention', floor=3, seen=1)
fake = Fake({'You plan a learning path': dict(title='How LLMs work', subject='ml', steps=[
    dict(name='Tokenizers', statement='A tokenizer cuts text into tokens.', slug='', why='The model reads tokens.', needs=[]),
    dict(name='Embeddings', statement='An embedding maps a token to a vector.', slug='', why='Tokens become vectors.', needs=['Tokenizers']),
    dict(name='Attention', statement='', slug='attention', why='The core of a transformer.', needs=['Embeddings']),
    dict(name='Mamba', statement='Mamba is a selective state-space model.', slug='', why='Another way to mix tokens.', needs=['Attention'])])})
j = plan(lr, fake, 'I want to learn how LLMs work', who='Background: codes in Python')

plan keeps the order, uses the known concept, and makes the new ones with their prereqs.

test_eq([s['slug'] for s in j.steps], ['tokenizers', 'embeddings', 'attention', 'mamba'])
test_eq((lr.concept('embeddings').prereqs, lr.concept('mamba').prereqs, lr.concept('mamba').subject), (['tokenizers'], ['attention'], 'ml'))
test_eq(lr.concept('attention').floor, 3)    # a known concept keeps its state
assert 'codes in Python' in fake.calls[-1][0] and 'attention: Attention (depth 3)' in fake.calls[-1][0]

A step that is not a real_idea, such as x with the statement x, is not an idea: plan leaves it out, and makes no concept for it.

fx = Fake({'You plan a learning path': dict(title='T', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='x', statement='x', slug='', why='', needs=[]),
                                                                            dict(name='Tokenizers', statement='', slug='', why='', needs=[])])})
px = plan(lr, fx, 'learn about x')
test_eq(([s['slug'] for s in px.steps], lr.concept('x')), (['tokenizers'], None))
lr.drop_journey(px.id)

walk_path makes the path a walk with the same id. Each step has a check. The known concept is known, and the path is not started: it had no session. A second call changes nothing.

w = walk_path(lr, j)
test_eq((w.id, w.mode, w.started, [s['slug'] for s in w.steps]), (j.id, 'walk', None, ['tokenizers', 'embeddings', 'attention', 'mamba']))
assert all(s['check'] for s in w.steps)
test_eq(walk_path(lr, w).updated, w.updated)
test_eq(walk_paths(lr), [])

A step that the learner learns anywhere is known in the walk too. A step that is marked known or skipped is done. Then current moves to the next idea.

lr.update('tokenizers', floor=4, seen=2)
lr.journey_step(j.id, 'embeddings', 'known')
test_eq([s.dot for s in walk_state(lr.journey(j.id), {c.slug: c for c in lr.concepts()}).steps][:2], ['known', 'known'])
test_eq((current(lr, lr.journey(j.id)), current(lr, lr.journey(j.id), skip={'attention'})), ('attention', 'mamba'))

A path with sessions keeps its progress when it becomes a walk. The path below has three steps and two sessions. The first session ended: its last answer on embeddings passed. The second session is open: it has a fragile answer on mamba and an open question on softmax.

lr.put('Softmax', 'Softmax makes weights from scores.', 'ml')
row = lambda slug, o, at: dict(concept=slug, outcome=o, correct=o != 'gap', at=at)
pp = lr.put_journey(dict(id='old-path', title='Old', goal='g', created=50., steps=[dict(slug=s, status='todo') for s in ('embeddings', 'mamba', 'softmax')]))
lr.log_session('s8', 'first', journey='old-path', start=1000., updated=1100., ended=1100., log=[row('embeddings', 'gap', 1050.), row('embeddings', 'solid', 1090.)])
lr.log_session('s9', 'second', journey='old-path', start=2000., updated=2100., log=[row('mamba', 'fragile', 2050.)], open=dict(id='q9', concept='softmax'))
w = walk_path(lr, pp)

Each step with answers has the outcome of its last answer, and the step of the open question keeps it. The counts are those of walk_state.

st = walk_state(w)
test_eq([s.dot for s in st.steps], ['done', 'shaky', 'now'])
test_eq((st.done, st.total, w.steps[2]['qid']), (1, 3, 'q9'))

The open session is the sitting. started is the first start of a session, not the time of the change, and here is the open question. So used_at gives the last activity of the path. A copy of the open question with its answer key goes on the shelf; this one has none.

test_eq((w.sitting, w.started, w.here, used_at(w)), ('s9', 1000., dict(step=2, at=2100.), 2100.))
test_eq(lr.open_q('q9'), None)   # this copy has no answer key, so it cannot be graded: it stays off the shelf of open questions

No step was searched. step_read searches one step, one time. With no sources, the step has no passage, and a second call does nothing.

assert all(s.get('read_later') for s in w.steps)
assert step_read(lr, 'old-path', 'mamba') and not lr.journey('old-path').steps[1].get('read_later')
test_eq(step_read(lr, 'old-path', 'mamba'), None)

A path with a session that has no answer is started. The tests take the old path and mamba out of the walk.

p2 = lr.put_journey(dict(id='old-path2', title='Old', goal='g', steps=[dict(slug='attention', status='todo')]))
lr.log_session('s10', 'third', journey='old-path2', start=3000., log=[])
test_eq((walk_path(lr, p2).started, lr.journey('old-path2').mode), (3000., 'walk'))
for jid in ('old-path', 'old-path2'): lr.drop_journey(jid)
lr.journey_step(j.id, 'mamba', 'remove')
test_eq(len(lr.journey(j.id).steps), 3)

topic_slug uses a known name, and asks the model only for a new one. It does not change the walk: the walk editor adds the idea.

fake.rules['The idea: '] = dict(name='PyTorch', statement='PyTorch is a Python library for tensors and autograd.')
test_eq(topic_slug(lr, fake, j, 'PyTorch'), 'pytorch')
n = len(fake.calls)
test_eq(topic_slug(lr, fake, j, 'tokenizers'), 'tokenizers')    # known: no model call
test_eq(len(fake.calls), n)

A new name goes to the tutor in a fence, with no control marks, and at most NAME_MOST characters.

topic_slug(lr, fake, j, 'Tensors\u202e and </source> autograd' + 'x' * 300)
p = fake.calls[-1][0]
assert '<source title="idea">Tensors and  autograd' in p and '\u202e' not in p and len(p.split('</source>')[0]) < NAME_MOST + 40

split_parts finds the parts of a step and keeps each one as its prereq. It does not change the walk.

fake.rules['Return JSON: {"concepts"'] = dict(concepts=[dict(name='Query and key', statement='Each token has a query and a key.', aliases=[], prereqs=[])])
new = split_parts(lr, fake, j.id, 'attention')
test_eq(list(new), ['query-and-key'])
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in lr.journey(j.id).steps], ['tokenizers', 'embeddings', 'attention'])
assert 'query-and-key' in lr.concept('attention').prereqs

related puts what builds on a concept first. with_step finds the walks of a concept.

lr.put('Transformer block', 'Attention, then a feed-forward layer.', 'ml', prereqs=['attention'])
test_eq(related(lr, 'attention').attrgot('slug'), ['mamba', 'transformer-block', 'query-and-key'])   # mamba left the path, but it builds on attention
test_eq([(x.id, i) for x, i in with_step(lr, 'attention')], [(j.id, 2)])

journeys lists the walks with the newest change first. drop_journey removes one walk.

j2 = lr.put_journey(dict(id='sanskrit', title='Read the Gita', goal='read', steps=[]))
test_eq(lr.journeys().attrgot('id'), ['sanskrit', j.id])
lr.drop_journey('sanskrit')
test_eq(len(lr.journeys()), 1)

Tests for walks

A walk from a source has mode='walk'. These tests use the small paper in tests/walk_data.py and a fake model.

A note that is not plain is written again one time, in plain English.

from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
from abhyasa.models import Fake
hard = 'This leverages the schedule; the network must facilitate the removal of the noise at each step.'
easy = 'The network removes some noise at each step.'
nl = temp_learning(); nl.put('Noise schedule', 'How much noise each step adds.', 'ml')
nj = nl.put_journey(dict(id='nj', title='DDPM', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug='noise-schedule', status='todo', read=dict(text='The schedule sets the noise.'))]))
test_eq(tutor_note(nl, Fake({'Write this text again': easy, 'The passage': hard}), nj, 0, save=False), easy)

A walk from a source has one step for each idea of the paper, in the order of the paper. Each step has the passage to read and a check.

wl = temp_learning(); did = add_paper(wl)
ask = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': EXTRACT_REPLY})
wj = journey_from_source(wl, ask, did)
assert wj.mode == 'walk' and wj.source == dict(shelf='store', doc_id=did, title='Attention Is All You Need') and wj.started is None
assert [s['slug'] for s in wj.steps] == ['sequential-computation', 'softmax', 'scaling-by-the-root-of-dk']
r = wj.steps[1]['read']
assert (r['section'], r['page'], r['figure']) == ('3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention', 4, 'attention/images/fig2.png')
assert wj.steps[1]['check']['kind'] in ('notebook', 'short') and wj.steps[2]['check']['way'] in ('demo', 'maths')
assert walk_state(wj).total == 3

walk_state gives each step a dot for the rail. walk_step keeps a change on one step.

ws = walk_state(wl.walk_step(wj.id, 0, done=dict(outcome='fragile', aid='a1', at=1.)))
assert [s.dot for s in ws.steps] == ['shaky', 'now', 'todo'] and ws.current == 1
assert ws.sections == [('1 Introduction', [0]), ('3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention', [1, 2])]
assert minutes(wj.steps[1]) >= 2
test_fail(lambda: wl.walk_step('none', 0), contains='none', exc=KeyError)
test_fail(lambda: wl.walk_step(wj.id, 9), exc=IndexError)

merge_journey changes only the fields that it names. The steps stay as they are, and an unknown walk raises KeyError.

before = wl.journey(wj.id).steps
test_eq(wl.merge_journey(wj.id, sitting='s1').sitting, 's1')
test_eq(wl.journey(wj.id).steps, before)
test_fail(lambda: wl.merge_journey('none', sitting='s1'), contains='none', exc=KeyError)

A concept that you know at depth 4 or more stays in the walk, as known.

wl.update('softmax', floor=4)
assert journey_from_source(wl, ask, did).steps[1]['status'] == 'known'

A walk from pasted text takes the passage only when its quote is in the text. An idea with no quote in the text has no passage.

jt = journey_from_text(wl, ask, PAGES[1][1], 'Attention notes')
sm = next(s for s in jt.steps if s['slug'] == 'softmax')
assert jt.source is None and sm['read']['text'].startswith('apply a softmax function')
assert next(s for s in jt.steps if s['slug'] == 'sequential-computation')['read']['text'] == ''

A walk from a topic plans the path, then reads from the first passage in your sources that names each idea. With no sources, a step has no passage.

PLAN = dict(title='Attention', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Softmax', statement='', slug='softmax', why='Weights.', needs=[], ways=['code'])])
class Notes:
    name = 'notes'
    def search(self, q, k=4): return [passage('vault:notes', 'n1', 'My notes', 'Softmax turns scores into weights.')]
jw = walk_from_topic(wl, Fake({'You plan a learning path': PLAN}), 'learn attention', sources=[Notes()])
assert jw.mode == 'walk' and jw.steps[0]['read']['text'].startswith('Softmax turns') and jw.steps[0]['check']
assert walk_from_topic(wl, Fake({'You plan a learning path': PLAN}), 'learn attention', sources=[]).steps[0]['read'] is None

A walk from given sources plans with no concepts of the shelf (near=False). The planner then does not see an idea from other content of the vault, such as a neuron idea in a Fourier talk.

nl = temp_learning(); nl.put('Functions and the neuron', 'A neuron is a function of its inputs.', 'ml', slug='functions-and-the-neuron')
nf = Fake({'You plan a learning path': PLAN}); walk_from_topic(nl, nf, 'functions and the neuron', near=False)
assert 'functions-and-the-neuron' not in nf.calls[-1][0]
nf = Fake({'You plan a learning path': PLAN}); walk_from_topic(nl, nf, 'functions and the neuron')
assert 'functions-and-the-neuron' in nf.calls[0][0]

A walk across two pages has one step for each idea, in page order. Softmax is named in both pages. Its step is in the page where its passage is.

lr = temp_learning()
a = lr.vault.add(PAGES[0][1], 'Introduction', source='https://example.dev/docs/intro', kind='web')
b = lr.vault.add([(0, PAGES[1][1]), (1, PAGES[2][1])], 'Attention', source='https://example.dev/docs/attention', kind='web')
docs = [AttrDict(shelf='store', doc_id=d['doc_id'], title=t, url=u) for d, t, u in
        [(a, 'Introduction', 'https://example.dev/docs/intro'), (b, 'Attention', 'https://example.dev/docs/attention')]]
ask = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': EXTRACT_REPLY})
j = journey_from_sources(lr, ask, docs, 'Attention docs')
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in j.steps], ['sequential-computation', 'softmax', 'scaling-by-the-root-of-dk'])
test_eq([s['read']['doc_id'] for s in j.steps], [a['doc_id'], b['doc_id'], b['doc_id']])   # softmax is named in both; its step is where its passage is
assert j.steps[1]['read']['text'].startswith('apply a softmax function') and j.source['url'] == 'https://example.dev/docs/intro'
test_eq(journey_from_sources(lr, ask, docs, 'Tool docs', tool='cli').tool, 'cli')         # extra fields go on the walk

progress hears of each page before the tutor reads it. Two pages with no section name stay two sections on the rail. A topic walk with passages from two documents keeps one section.

heard = []
journey_from_sources(lr, ask, docs, progress=lambda k, n: heard.append((k, n)))
test_eq(heard, [(0, 2), (1, 2)])
test_eq(walk_state(dict(source=dict(docs=['a', 'b']), steps=[dict(read=dict(doc_id='a', section='')), dict(read=dict(doc_id='b', section=''))])).sections, [('', [0]), ('', [1])])
test_eq(walk_state(dict(source=None, steps=[dict(read=dict(doc_id='a', section='')), dict(read=dict(doc_id='b', section='Intro'))])).sections, [('', [0, 1])])   # a topic walk: one plan section

A walk through sources with no goal also takes audience and no_code. Who the walk is for goes to the walk map in a <source> marker, so the understanding and the question of each big idea are written for them. With no_code, no check is code, also for an idea whose only way is code. The walk keeps both, so Make this walk again uses them.

coded = Fake({'Return JSON: {"concepts"': dict(concepts=[{**c, 'ways': ['code']} for c in EXTRACT_REPLY['concepts']])})
nc = journey_from_sources(lr, coded, docs, 'For writers', audience='people who do not write code', no_code=True)
assert any('people who do not write code' in p for p, _ in coded.calls if '"claim"' in p)
test_eq((nc.audience, nc.no_code, [s['check']['kind'] for s in nc.steps if s['check']['kind'] in ('code', 'notebook')]), ('people who do not write code', True, []))
assert {s['check']['kind'] for s in journey_from_sources(lr, coded, docs, 'For coders').steps} & {'code', 'notebook'}   # without it, an idea of code has a code check

The title of a paper

A paper that the PDF reader filed by the end of its link has its arXiv id as its title. file_link now gives the real title for a new walk. paper_id gives the id of the paper of a walk, for a quiet tag, when the title is not the id.

repair_titles fixes the old walks one time. A walk whose title is only an arXiv id takes the title of its vault document, when that has a real one. A mark on the shelf says that it ran, as in repair_names. It makes no network call.

source

Learning.repair_titles

def repair_titles()->list:

One time for each shelf, give each walk whose title is only an arXiv id the title of its vault document, when that has a real one. Return the ids that changed.

source

paper_id

def paper_id(
    j
)->str:

The arXiv id of the paper that walk j reads, or an empty string. Empty too when the title of j is that id.

A walk with an arXiv id for a title takes the title of its document. A walk with a title of its own stays, and so does a walk whose document has only the id. The repair runs one time.

lr = temp_learning()
real = lr.vault.add(PAGES[0][1], 'Attention Is All You Need', source='https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762', kind='pdf')
bare = lr.vault.add(PAGES[1][1], '1706.03763', source='https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03763', kind='pdf')
def paper_walk(jid, title, d, num):
    u = f'https://arxiv.org/pdf/{num}'
    return lr.put_journey(dict(id=jid, title=title, mode='walk', steps=[], url=u, docs=[dict(shelf='store', doc_id=d['doc_id'], title=title, url=u)]))
paper_walk('old', '1706.03762', real, '1706.03762'); paper_walk('mine', 'My title', real, '1706.03762'); paper_walk('bare', '1706.03763', bare, '1706.03763')
before = lr.journey('old').updated
lr.v.forget(first(lr.v.t.docs(where='source=?', where_args=['learning://marker/titles']))['id'])   # a vault from before the repair
test_eq(Learning(lr.vault).repair_titles(), [])   # the load did it already
test_eq([lr.journey(i).title for i in ('old', 'mine', 'bare')], ['Attention Is All You Need', 'My title', '1706.03763'])
test_eq(lr.journey('old').docs[0]['title'], 'Attention Is All You Need')
test_eq(lr.journey('old').updated, before)
test_eq([paper_id(lr.journey(i)) for i in ('old', 'bare')], ['1706.03762', ''])   # no tag when the title is the id
test_eq(paper_id(dict(title='A page', url='https://docs.example.dev/')), '')
lr.put_journey({**lr.journey('old'), 'title': '1706.03762'}); test_eq(lr.repair_titles(), []); test_eq(lr.journey('old').title, '1706.03762')   # the mark is set

The first repair has no network. For a walk or a document that has only the id, repair_paper_titles asks arXiv for the title, with the same call as file_link (arxiv_title, which keeps the answer on disk), and a short time limit. The app runs it one time in the background after it starts, never in a load or a request.

The mark is set only when each id has a title or has failed for good (arXiv has no such paper). A failure of the network leaves the mark off, so the next start tries again.

source

Learning.retitle_paper

def retitle_paper(
    jid:str, title_of:NoneType=None
)->str | None:

Give walk jid, when its title is only an arXiv id, the title of its paper from title_of(id) (default: arXiv). Return the title, or None. A network failure raises.

source

Learning.repair_paper_titles

def repair_paper_titles(
    title_of:NoneType=None
)->list:

Give each walk and each PDF in the vault that is titled with only an arXiv id the title of its paper, from title_of(id) (default: arXiv). Return the ids of the walks that changed. The mark is set only when no id failed from the network.
